Cross-validation for bridge regression

Source: R/cv.bridge.R
cv.bridge.Rd

Evaluate a fitted penalty path using contiguous validation folds and return the full-data coefficients together with two penalty selectors.

Usage

cv.bridge(
  X,
  y,
  q,
  lambda,
  nfolds = 10,
  lambda.min = ifelse(n > p, 0.001, 0.05),
  nlambda = 100,
  eta = 1e-07,
  converge = 10^10,
  num_threads = 10
)

Arguments

X

Numeric design matrix with n observation rows and p predictor columns. Supply finite values and predictors with nonzero variation; omit an intercept column. A data frame is converted using model.matrix(~0+., X); restrictions and future predictions must use the resulting predictor order.

y

Numeric response vector of length n, containing finite values.

q

Bridge-penalty exponent, a finite number in (0, 2]. Values 1 and 2 specify the L1 and L2 penalty forms. Estimation uses local quadratic approximation (LQA).

lambda

Optional nonempty numeric vector of finite, nonnegative penalty values. Its order is retained. When supplied, it determines the fitted path and overrides nlambda and the grid argument lambda.min.

nfolds

Number of validation folds, an integer between 2 and n. The default is 10.

lambda.min

Positive absolute endpoint of the automatically generated penalty grid. The default is 0.001 when n > p, and 0.05 otherwise. This argument is a penalty value, not a ratio. In CV results, the field also named lambda.min instead denotes the selected penalty.

nlambda

Number of automatically generated penalty values, an integer of at least 2. The default is 100; ignored when lambda is supplied.

eta

Positive numerical tolerance, with default 1e-7. Used for coefficient elimination and stopping on squared coefficient changes.

converge

Nonnegative initial convergence-distance value, retained for compatibility. The default is 1e10. Iteration stops when the updated squared coefficient change is at most eta, or at the historical cap.

num_threads

Requested fold-level workers, a positive integer. The default is 10; the effective count is capped at nfolds. Builds without OpenMP execute folds sequentially. Use rbridge_info() to inspect the compiled support.

Value

A list of class cv.bridge with components:

cve

Numeric vector of validation mean squared errors, one per penalty. Squared holdout residuals are summed across folds and divided by the total observation count, so each observation has the same weight.

cvse

Numeric vector from the historical CV error-bar calculation. It is not the conventional standard error of foldwise mean squared errors.

cvup, cvlo

Upper and lower curves, computed as cve + cvse and cve - cvse.

lambda

Numeric penalty vector in fitted order.

nz

Number of nonzero slopes, excluding the intercept, in each full-data fit.

betas

Full-data coefficient matrix with p + 1 rows and length(lambda) columns. The first row is (Intercept); the remaining rows are original-scale slopes in predictor order.

lambda.min

Fitted penalty with the smallest cve. Ties select the largest penalty among the minimizers. This selected value is distinct from the input argument specifying the generated grid endpoint.

lambda.1se

Largest fitted penalty whose cve is no greater than cve + cvse evaluated at the selected lambda.min. The name follows the historical convention; the threshold uses the package's cvse calculation described above.

Details

Fold assignment follows the supplied row order. The nfolds validation sets are contiguous blocks; their sizes can differ by one. Centering and RMS scaling use all observations before fold allocation, and each fold fit also reconstructs its training-set intercept. These historical preprocessing and error-bar conventions are retained. The reported validation error aggregates held-out predictions at each fitted penalty, and coefficients in betas come from a final fit to all observations.

For one fixed penalty, let KK be nfolds, nn the total observation count, IkI_k the validation indices in fold kk, and eie_i the held-out response residual for observation ii. Equation (1) defines a fold's error contribution dkd_k, the pooled validation MSE, and the historical error-bar width: dk=1n∑i∈Ikei2,cve=∑k=1Kdk,cvse=1K(n−1)∑k=1K(dk−cve)2.(1) \begin{aligned} d_k&=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\in I_k}e_i^2,\\ \mathrm{cve}&=\sum_{k=1}^{K}d_k,\\ \mathrm{cvse}&=\sqrt{\frac{1}{K(n-1)} \sum_{k=1}^{K}(d_k-\mathrm{cve})^2}. \qquad (1) \end{aligned} The folds partition all observations, so the sum in Equation (1) weights each held-out observation equally. The final quantity supplies the plotted bar width and the historical lambda.1se threshold. Its centering uses the pooled cve, not the average fold contribution, and it is not a conventional foldwise standard error.

predict() defaults to the minimum-error penalty lambda.min. coef() defaults to lambda.1se. Supply s explicitly to use the same penalty for both operations. Use plot() to inspect the curve, error bars and selected penalties.

Examples

# Reproducible synthetic demonstration: 100 observations, eight predictors.
set.seed(2019)
beta <- c(3, 1.5, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0)
p <- length(beta)
beta <- matrix(beta, nrow = p, ncol = 1)
n <- 100
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), nrow = n, ncol = p)
y <- as.numeric(X %*% beta + rnorm(n))

# Five penalties keep this help example fast; the default is 100.
# Three contiguous folds and one worker keep this demonstration small.
model1 <- cv.bridge(X, y, q = 1,
                     nlambda = 5, nfolds = 3, num_threads = 1)
model2 <- cv.bridge(X, y, q = 2,
                     nlambda = 5, nfolds = 3, num_threads = 1)
# Inspect both selectors and explicitly choose the minimum-error fit.
c(minimum_error = model1$lambda.min, historical_1se = model1$lambda.1se)
#>  minimum_error historical_1se 
#>      0.0010000      0.8956281 
coef(model1, s = "lambda.min")
#>                   0.001
#> (Intercept)  0.02436200
#> V1           2.97264933
#> V2           1.57302384
#> V3           0.07468856
#> V4          -0.08748886
#> V5           1.98528242
#> V6          -0.09864804
#> V7           0.07149838
#> V8          -0.02593340
predict(model1, newx = X[1:5, , drop = FALSE], s = "lambda.min")
#> [1]  -1.4546979   0.3068586  -1.5652478   2.6580196 -10.4100022
plot(model1)
